goal: Homepage complete with zero projects; event format and lifecycle change content and layout.
note: All proposed challenges, schedules, venues and projects are illustrative. Challenge/schedule content availability needs confirmation before implementation.

prompts.prompt:
Design a high-fidelity UI concept board for HackJudge's adaptive HOMEPAGE. Wide landscape board, exactly two desktop website views side by side at equal scale, labeled "Before the event · No projects" and "During the event · First submissions". Header for both: HackJudge wordmark, Events, right Sign in. Above the board a small note "Design concept · All event details and projects are sample content". Sharp professional flat web design, no devices/perspective. Strong recognizable identity across both views: white/off-white neutral canvas, dark ink, confident condensed sans headings, normal readable sans text, crisp fine rules, minimal 6px rounding, localized color, no soft biomedical green, no gradients, generic icon card soup, dashboards, marketing hero slogans, abstract cover art or photos used to disguise missing content. User wants visually appealing technical competition platform. Both are HOMEPAGES led by focal event, not all-events directory. Before event MUST HAVE ZERO PROJECTS, ZERO team names, ZERO screenshots, ZERO fake counts/award totals or a placeholder gallery. Show a purposeful full composition made of event-owned information. Event stage and dates should be obvious and actions appropriate: "View event" and "How to participate" before, event participation actions during only if sample state supports them. Same sample focal event remains on both views. Secondary "On the calendar" strip low on page with two next events and "All events". During begins with just TWO submitted projects, name and short description ONLY. NO project images, fake repositories or screenshots: demonstrate graceful minimal submissions. Show stage text clearly "Projects arriving", and do not assume all submissions or judging ready. A compact plain line says "Judging opens after submissions close" for hackathons, analogous not-yet-open voting/appreciation for other modes. IMPORTANT no empty state as main visual, no fabricated project showcase before the event; content gives the homepage energy even with zero projects. Keep text legible and design mature yet distinctive.
Title board "Hackathon / Challenge-led homepage". Accent vivid deep cobalt. Sample event CivicHacks 2026, October 12, Innovation Center. Before: compact stage strip upcoming and date, left third strong stacked CivicHacks 2026 title 58px, useful short description "Build practical tools for stronger communities.", date/location, View event action. Right two-thirds dominant ink-dark 'The challenges' board holding three substantial horizontal text rows: 'Energy & climate' with 'Help communities use resources more effectively.', 'Access & inclusion' with 'Make everyday services easier to reach.', 'Public life' with 'Improve the places people share.'. Each row uses a restrained cobalt/cool offwhite number or category chip as actual track identity, different text sizes balanced with generous space, no icons and no arbitrary section numbering. Below full-width build-day timeline with chronological times 09:00 Kickoff, 10:00 Build, 15:00 Submit, 16:00 Demo. All illustrative. Compact judging method region 'Innovation / Impact / Execution', factual no fake weights. During: same header and left event identity but stage 'Building is underway', timeline highlights Build, clear deadline 15:00. Top right retains the challenge board in a smaller useful composition, lower right 'Projects arriving' with two plain substantive rows 'Voltify / Community energy-demand forecasting' and 'AgriSense / Field sensors and crop insights', track names; no giant gallery or blank thumbnails. View event action visible, 'Judging opens after submissions close'. Keep the before view visually complete and stronger than generic event announcement; use the timeline and dark track board as focal composition.

Title board "Demo Day / Visit-led homepage". Accent strong vermilion #C94622; ink and white shared platform. Sample event Fall Demo Day, October 25, Innovation Center. Before: broad event masthead 54px Fall Demo Day, stage Upcoming, succinct 'A day to meet the builders and see their work.', date/location, View event. Below broad two-thirds open editorial schedule composition with readable headings: 'Make a day of it', 13:00 Doors open, 13:30 Project demonstrations, 15:30 Community appreciation, 16:00 Wrap-up. Schedule is generous table/rhythm not tiny cards. Adjacent a locally warm pale orange region 'Visit. Ask. Appreciate.' explains browse booths, talk to teams, give appreciations when event opens. Lower area 'For visitors / For teams' divided plainly with useful arrival and submission instructions. NO projects or photos before. During: same masthead with Live, useful schedule retains prominence, body opens small 2-item project list 'Voltify / Community energy-demand forecasting', 'AgriSense / Field sensors and crop insights', only names descriptions and team-free plain text; heading 'Projects arriving'. Side panel 'Your visit' holds location schedule details and how appreciation works with 'Appreciations open at 15:30'. No live appreciation hearts/counters. Visual transition from useful visit planner to an early modest exhibition while keeping shared identity and confident typography.

Title board "Code & Tell / Session-led homepage". Accent deep violet #7041BD; same white/ink platform. Sample event Code & Tell, November 9, Innovation Center. Before: main typography composition with large 60px Code & Tell, subline 'Bring what you’re working on.', Upcoming stage date/location, View event button. Right main composition a simple session agenda on white with generous violet fine dividers: 17:00 Welcome, 17:15 Short demos, 18:00 Audience ballot, 18:15 Wrap-up. Lower wide localized pale lilac region 'A small demo is enough.' with exactly two substantial plain content columns 'Present / Show what you built, explain one decision, share what you learned.' and 'Join in / Watch the demos, ask questions, choose your favorites when voting opens.' These are instructions, not marketing filler. NO invented presenters/projects before, no ranked ballot. During: same heading with 'Session underway', agenda highlights Short demos, body a presentation-order list heading 'What’s being shared', with two entries labeled presentation order not rank: 01 Voltify / Community energy-demand forecasting and 02 AgriSense / Field sensors and crop insights. No media. A concise aside 'Voting opens at 18:00', neutral 'Projects arriving' status, View event action. Keep agenda present rather than replace whole site; distinctive structured text-led layout with purposeful violet accents. Both should be visually appealing with absolutely zero required project images.
